2. In `app.py`, the `logger` property calls `create_logger(self)`.

3. Since the logger is always named `"flask.app"`, both `app1` and `app2` get the SAME logger instance from Python's logging module. When you add handlers to `app1.logger`, then later to `app2.logger`, they both refer to the same logger object with the name "flask.app", so both handlers end up on the same logger.

This is the bug. The fix would be to give each Flask app its own logger, perhaps by using the app's name (or import name) as part of the logger name, e.g., `logging.getLogger(f"flask.app.{app.import_name}")` or similar.
